concepts.label: Agent architecture
concepts.definition: Combine a model, tools, memory, control flow, and an environment into an agent.

concepts.label: Workflows versus agents
concepts.definition: Distinguish fixed program control flow from model-directed control flow.

concepts.label: Multi-step reasoning
concepts.definition: Use intermediate reasoning steps to solve a task.

concepts.label: Chain of thought
concepts.definition: Generate intermediate reasoning steps before a final answer.

concepts.label: Self-consistency
concepts.definition: Sample several reasoning paths and combine their answers.

concepts.label: Reflection and self-correction
concepts.definition: Use feedback about an attempt to revise reasoning or future actions.

concepts.label: Reflexion
concepts.definition: Store verbal feedback from earlier attempts to improve later attempts.

concepts.label: Planning and task decomposition
concepts.definition: Choose and organize steps or subtasks before or during action.

concepts.label: ReAct
concepts.definition: Alternate reasoning, tool actions, and observations.

concepts.label: CodeAct
concepts.definition: Use executable code as the agent action interface.

concepts.label: Plan then execute
concepts.definition: Separate a planning stage from the execution of the planned steps.

concepts.label: Prompt chaining
concepts.definition: Pass the output of one model step into the next step.

concepts.label: Routing
concepts.definition: Choose a specialized path or component for an input.

concepts.label: Parallel execution
concepts.definition: Run independent tasks at the same time and combine results.

concepts.label: Orchestrator and workers
concepts.definition: Let a coordinator split work and assign subtasks to worker agents.

concepts.label: Evaluator and optimizer loop
concepts.definition: Use a separate evaluator to guide repeated improvement of an output.

concepts.label: Language model foundations
concepts.definition: Explain next-token modeling and the main parts of a language model.

concepts.label: Transformer and attention
concepts.definition: Use attention-based neural networks to model token sequences.

concepts.label: Decoding and sampling
concepts.definition: Choose output tokens from model probabilities.

concepts.label: Structured output and constrained decoding
concepts.definition: Constrain model output to a schema or a set of valid tokens.

concepts.label: Inference-time scaling
concepts.definition: Spend more inference compute on reasoning, search, or repeated attempts.

concepts.label: Prompt design
concepts.definition: Design instructions, examples, and role messages to guide a model.

concepts.label: Few-shot prompting
concepts.definition: Include examples in a prompt to guide the response.

concepts.label: Automatic prompt optimization
concepts.definition: Use measured feedback to search for better instructions or examples.

concepts.label: Supervised fine-tuning
concepts.definition: Train a model on examples of desired responses or action trajectories.

concepts.label: Model training and post-training
concepts.definition: Train model weights before or after initial pretraining.

concepts.label: Reinforcement learning
concepts.definition: Learn a policy by using rewards from interaction.

concepts.label: Proximal policy optimization
concepts.definition: Update a policy with a clipped objective to limit policy changes.

concepts.label: Group relative policy optimization
concepts.definition: Compare rewards within groups of sampled outputs to update a policy.

concepts.label: Knowledge distillation
concepts.definition: Train a model to follow the outputs or behavior of a teacher model.

concepts.label: Retrieval-augmented generation
concepts.definition: Retrieve external information and use it to generate an answer.

concepts.label: Document chunking and indexing
concepts.definition: Split source documents and build an index for retrieval.

concepts.label: Embedding-based retrieval
concepts.definition: Encode queries and documents as vectors and retrieve similar documents.

concepts.label: Sparse retrieval
concepts.definition: Rank documents with token-based relevance scores.

concepts.label: Hybrid retrieval
concepts.definition: Combine lexical and embedding-based retrieval results.

concepts.label: Reranking and late interaction
concepts.definition: Rescore retrieved candidates with richer query-document comparisons.

concepts.label: Graph-based retrieval
concepts.definition: Use graph relations or graph summaries to support retrieval.

concepts.label: Agentic retrieval
concepts.definition: Let an agent decide when and how to retrieve and revise a search.

concepts.label: Retrieval evaluation
concepts.definition: Measure whether retrieval returns relevant evidence.

concepts.label: Tool use and function calling
concepts.definition: Let a model choose and call external functions and consume their results.

concepts.label: Tool discovery and selection
concepts.definition: Find and select relevant tools from available tool descriptions.

concepts.label: Model Context Protocol
concepts.definition: Connect agent hosts and tool servers through a shared tool interface.

concepts.label: Tool-call evaluation
concepts.definition: Check selected tools, arguments, execution, and tool-use outcomes.

concepts.label: Agent frameworks and orchestration
concepts.definition: Use reusable components and control flow to build agent systems.

concepts.label: DSPy
concepts.definition: Build and optimize language model programs with signatures, modules, and optimizers.

concepts.label: LangGraph
concepts.definition: Build stateful model workflows with nodes, edges, and graph state.

concepts.label: Agent harness design
concepts.definition: Design the runtime around a model, including tools, state, limits, and execution.

concepts.label: Durable execution and recovery
concepts.definition: Persist execution state and recover work after failures or pauses.

concepts.label: Tracing and observability
concepts.definition: Record agent steps and inspect behavior, failures, and runtime measurements.

concepts.label: Context engineering
concepts.definition: Select and organize the information supplied to a model for each step.

concepts.label: Context summarization and compaction
concepts.definition: Replace long interaction history with a shorter useful representation.

concepts.label: Context offloading
concepts.definition: Store information outside the active prompt and load it when needed.

concepts.label: Observation masking
concepts.definition: Remove or hide older tool outputs while keeping useful interaction structure.

concepts.label: Context isolation
concepts.definition: Give a task or subagent a separate context to limit interference.

concepts.label: Progressive disclosure
concepts.definition: Load instructions or tool details only when the current task needs them.

concepts.label: Agent memory
concepts.definition: Store and reuse information across steps or interactions.

concepts.label: Working memory
concepts.definition: Keep information needed for the current task in active context.

concepts.label: Episodic memory
concepts.definition: Store events or past experiences that an agent can recall.

concepts.label: Semantic memory
concepts.definition: Store facts and general knowledge for later use.

concepts.label: Procedural memory and skills
concepts.definition: Store reusable procedures or skills that guide actions.

concepts.label: Tiered memory
concepts.definition: Move information between memory levels with different capacity and access costs.

concepts.label: Memory maintenance and consolidation
concepts.definition: Update, combine, remove, or reorganize stored memories.

concepts.label: Memory evaluation
concepts.definition: Measure recall, updating, temporal reasoning, and useful memory use.

concepts.label: Multi-agent systems
concepts.definition: Use several agents that interact to solve tasks.

concepts.label: Agent handoffs
concepts.definition: Transfer control and relevant information from one agent to another.

concepts.label: Agent as a tool
concepts.definition: Call a specialist agent as a tool while the caller keeps control.

concepts.label: Shared memory and task coordination
concepts.definition: Coordinate agents through shared state, task records, or message stores.

concepts.label: Agent2Agent protocol
concepts.definition: Describe and exchange tasks between agents through a shared protocol.

concepts.label: Workspace isolation
concepts.definition: Give agents separate working directories to prevent conflicting file changes.

concepts.label: Multi-agent failure analysis
concepts.definition: Analyze coordination failures, conflicting goals, and harmful group behavior.

concepts.label: Training data selection and quality
concepts.definition: Select and check useful tasks, demonstrations, and trajectories.

concepts.label: Synthetic data and trajectory generation
concepts.definition: Generate tasks, examples, or agent rollouts for training or testing.

concepts.label: Human demonstrations and feedback
concepts.definition: Collect human actions or feedback to train or improve an agent.

concepts.label: Agent evaluation and benchmarks
concepts.definition: Measure agent behavior and outcomes with defined tasks and scores.

concepts.label: Benchmark and test-set design
concepts.definition: Define tasks, environments, stopping rules, and scoring for evaluation.

concepts.label: Code-based evaluators
concepts.definition: Use deterministic code or tests to score agent behavior or outputs.

concepts.label: Human evaluation
concepts.definition: Use human judgments or labels to assess agent behavior or outputs.

concepts.label: LLM as a judge
concepts.definition: Use a language model to score another system with stated criteria.

concepts.label: Judge validation and bias
concepts.definition: Check evaluator agreement, accuracy, and bias against trusted labels.

concepts.label: Evaluation rubrics
concepts.definition: Define explicit criteria and rating rules for judgments.

concepts.label: Reliability and repeated-run evaluation
concepts.definition: Measure variation and success across repeated agent runs.

concepts.label: Reward hacking and evaluation gaming
concepts.definition: Exploit a reward or scoring rule without meeting the intended task.

concepts.label: Coding and terminal agents
concepts.definition: Use agents to write, edit, test, or run code and command-line tasks.

concepts.label: Agent safety and guardrails
concepts.definition: Limit harmful agent actions and enforce task or use constraints.

concepts.label: Prompt injection
concepts.definition: Untrusted content attempts to redirect an agent or override instructions.

concepts.label: Privacy and user data protection
concepts.definition: Control disclosure and use of private user information.

concepts.label: Sandboxed execution
concepts.definition: Run code or tools inside a restricted environment.

concepts.label: Human oversight and approval
concepts.definition: Pause or route an agent decision to a person for review or approval.

concepts.label: Personalization and user modeling
concepts.definition: Adapt agent behavior to a user's preferences, history, or needs.

concepts.label: Proactive and mixed-initiative agents
concepts.definition: Let an agent decide when to initiate useful actions or interaction.

concepts.label: Tokenization
concepts.definition: Convert text to token IDs and back using a defined vocabulary and algorithm.

concepts.label: Gradient descent and backpropagation
concepts.definition: Compute loss gradients and update neural-network weights.

concepts.label: Beam search
concepts.definition: Keep several high-scoring partial outputs during decoding.

concepts.label: Tree of thoughts
concepts.definition: Search a branching set of intermediate reasoning states.

concepts.label: Answer verification
concepts.definition: Check claims or candidate answers before accepting a result.

concepts.label: Soft prompt tuning
concepts.definition: Learn prompt embeddings while keeping the main model weights fixed.

concepts.label: Sliding-window conversation memory
concepts.definition: Keep only a recent window of interaction history in the prompt.

concepts.label: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
concepts.definition: Train a reward model from human preferences and use it to guide policy updates.

concepts.label: Direct preference optimization
concepts.definition: Train directly on preferred and rejected response pairs.

concepts.label: Reward modeling
concepts.definition: Learn or define a score that guides policy training.

concepts.label: Low-rank adaptation
concepts.definition: Adapt a model by training small low-rank weight updates.

concepts.label: Model compression and quantization
concepts.definition: Reduce model size or arithmetic precision to lower execution costs.

concepts.label: Response caching
concepts.definition: Reuse stored results for repeated model or tool requests.

concepts.label: Conversation and execution state
concepts.definition: Track messages, task progress, and runtime data across agent steps.

concepts.label: Error handling and retries
concepts.definition: Detect model or tool errors and retry, recover, or stop safely.

concepts.label: Long-horizon agent tasks
concepts.definition: Maintain progress over long sequences of dependent actions.

concepts.label: Threat modeling and least privilege
concepts.definition: Identify threats and limit access to the permissions a task requires.

concepts.label: Red teaming and adversarial evaluation
concepts.definition: Test an agent with attacks and difficult misuse cases.

concepts.label: Memory poisoning
concepts.definition: An attacker changes stored memory to affect later agent behavior.

concepts.label: Evidence grounding and hallucination control
concepts.definition: Tie claims to trusted evidence and reduce unsupported statements.

concepts.label: Abstention and uncertainty handling
concepts.definition: Decline to answer or ask for help when evidence or confidence is insufficient.

concepts.label: Persona and response style control
concepts.definition: Make an agent follow a defined identity and style while preserving factual constraints.

concepts.label: Computer-use and web agents
concepts.definition: Observe and operate browser or desktop interfaces to complete tasks.

concepts.label: Visual interface grounding
concepts.definition: Map a visual instruction or screen element to an actionable UI target.

concepts.label: Deep research agents
concepts.definition: Run repeated searches, inspect evidence, and synthesize a research answer.

concepts.label: Citation and evidence evaluation
concepts.definition: Check that references exist, support claims, and cover the answer.

concepts.label: Prompt prefix and KV caching
concepts.definition: Reuse attention keys and values or shared prompt prefixes to reduce inference work.

concepts.label: Long-context modeling
concepts.definition: Extend or manage model behavior on long input sequences.

concepts.label: Inference serving and performance
concepts.definition: Manage inference engines, batching, latency, throughput, and memory use.

concepts.label: Credit assignment and advantage estimation
concepts.definition: Estimate which actions contribute to reward and use baselines or value estimates.

concepts.label: Policy gradient methods
concepts.definition: Update a policy using gradients of expected reward.

concepts.label: Exploration and curriculum design
concepts.definition: Maintain useful policy exploration and select training tasks by difficulty.

concepts.label: Distributed and asynchronous RL systems
concepts.definition: Coordinate rollout generation, training engines, and policy synchronization.

concepts.label: Skill induction from experience
concepts.definition: Extract reusable procedures or code from prior task trajectories.

concepts.label: Checkpointing and resuming
concepts.definition: Save agent state so a thread or task can resume after interruption.

concepts.label: Trajectory and process evaluation
concepts.definition: Evaluate the sequence of agent decisions and actions rather than only the final output.

concepts.label: Regression and version comparison
concepts.definition: Compare agent versions on shared cases and detect behavior that became worse.

concepts.label: Best-of-N selection
concepts.definition: Generate several candidates and select one with a verifier or reward score.

concepts.label: Multi-agent debate
concepts.definition: Let several agents exchange arguments or critique candidate answers.

concepts.label: Asynchronous agent coordination
concepts.definition: Run agents concurrently and coordinate completion, progress, and results.

concepts.label: User and environment simulation
concepts.definition: Simulate interaction partners or environments for training and testing.

concepts.label: Human-agent collaboration
concepts.definition: Design how people and agents share tasks, control, and interaction.

concepts.label: Work automation and social impact
concepts.definition: Analyze how agent automation affects tasks, workers, and the design of work.

concepts.label: Model selection and provider integration
concepts.definition: Choose a model for capability, cost, privacy, and tool support and connect its API.

concepts.label: Agent filesystem and storage backends
concepts.definition: Expose file tools while controlling where files are stored and how they persist.

concepts.label: Embedded code interpreter
concepts.definition: Run generated code in an interpreter within the agent loop.

concepts.label: Programmatic tool composition
concepts.definition: Write code that calls and combines several tools in one execution.

concepts.label: Agent middleware
concepts.definition: Add reusable behavior around model calls, tool calls, and agent execution.

concepts.label: Tool authentication and credential handling
concepts.definition: Authenticate tool connections and control how credentials reach tools.

concepts.label: Agent deployment and service APIs
concepts.definition: Run an agent as a persistent service with APIs and supporting infrastructure.

concepts.label: Managed agent hosting
concepts.definition: Use a hosted service to run agents and provide storage, tools, and interfaces.

concepts.label: Dynamic subagent creation and batch delegation
concepts.definition: Create or schedule subagents for a changing list of work items.

concepts.label: Memory scoping and user isolation
concepts.definition: Keep persistent memories separate by user, thread, or workspace.

concepts.label: State replay and branching
concepts.definition: Inspect earlier checkpoints and resume or fork from a previous state.

concepts.label: Sales and business assistants
concepts.definition: Use an agent to manage customer requests, business data, reports, or messages.

concepts.label: Knowledge curation and synthesis
concepts.definition: Search, organize, compare, and combine information into an evidence-based account.

concepts.label: Perspective-guided research
concepts.definition: Use several viewpoints to generate questions and broaden evidence collection.

concepts.label: Decision rationale and data provenance
concepts.definition: Record where facts came from and how evidence and assumptions support a decision.

concepts.label: Formal reasoning with SMT
concepts.definition: Translate constraints to logic and use a satisfiability-modulo-theories solver.

concepts.label: Constraint-satisfaction retrieval
concepts.definition: Retrieve records whose formal constraints are satisfied instead of relying only on similarity.

concepts.label: Semantic parsing to formal queries
concepts.definition: Translate natural language to a formal query or logical representation.

concepts.label: Concept canonicalization and ontologies
concepts.definition: Map varied terms to shared concepts and logical relations.

concepts.label: Missing-data imputation and assumptions
concepts.definition: Fill missing facts using stated policies and expose the resulting assumptions.

concepts.label: Clinical decision and literature agents
concepts.definition: Use agents to analyze clinical evidence, compare patient findings, or match trial criteria.

concepts.label: Natural-language database and graph queries
concepts.definition: Use language models to query structured databases and knowledge graphs.

concepts.label: Queries over structured and unstructured data
concepts.definition: Compose database operations with free-text retrieval and language processing.

concepts.label: Dialogue state tracking and management
concepts.definition: Represent conversation facts, task state, and valid next actions.

concepts.label: Declarative task-oriented agent specifications
concepts.definition: Define task fields, constraints, and policies and let a runtime manage the dialogue.

concepts.label: Data-driven research and analysis
concepts.definition: Use queries and analysis to form, test, and explain findings from structured data.

concepts.label: Research result reproduction
concepts.definition: Reproduce published claims using source data and executable analysis.

concepts.label: Schema induction and information extraction
concepts.definition: Define or infer a structured schema and extract source evidence into it.

concepts.label: Database reconciliation and deduplication
concepts.definition: Resolve duplicate, conflicting, or partial extracted records while keeping provenance.

concepts.label: Vision-language models
concepts.definition: Use models that combine visual inputs and language outputs.

concepts.label: Historical document transcription
concepts.definition: Extract structured text and layout from scans of printed or handwritten documents.

concepts.label: Hypothesis and evidence ledger
concepts.definition: Track competing hypotheses, supporting evidence, refutations, and open questions.

concepts.label: Requirements and expected behavior
concepts.definition: Define observable agent behavior and expected outcomes before evaluating a system.

concepts.label: Error analysis and failure taxonomy
concepts.definition: Inspect failed cases, label failure types, and prioritize fixes by frequency and impact.

concepts.label: Multi-turn and session evaluation
concepts.definition: Evaluate behavior across conversation turns and preserve relevant earlier constraints.

concepts.label: Task outcome and state-change verification
concepts.definition: Check the actual system state and side effects after an agent acts.

concepts.label: Controlled improvement experiments
concepts.definition: Change a defined part of an agent and compare versions under the same test conditions.

concepts.label: Production monitoring and evaluation feedback
concepts.definition: Inspect real runs and feedback and turn production failures into test cases.

concepts.label: Evaluator precision, recall, and agreement
concepts.definition: Measure evaluator errors and agreement against trusted labels.

concepts.label: Cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs
concepts.definition: Compare performance gains with runtime cost, time, and failure consequences.

concepts.label: Self-play training
concepts.definition: Generate training challenges through interaction between agents or roles and learn from the resulting tasks.

concepts.label: Automatic harness improvement
concepts.definition: Search or revise agent runtime instructions and structure using measured feedback.

concepts.label: Agentic debugging and refactoring
concepts.definition: Use agents to locate bugs or change code structure while preserving required behavior.

concepts.label: Scientific workflow automation
concepts.definition: Use agents to configure and run scientific tools or experiments.

concepts.label: Developer-agent alignment
concepts.definition: Analyze whether an agent follows developer intent, constraints, and expected workflows.

concepts.label: Research design and paper critique
concepts.definition: Form research questions, assess prior work, design experiments, and report evidence.

concepts.label: Language model scaling laws
concepts.definition: Relate model performance to data size, parameter count, and compute budget.

concepts.label: Speculative decoding
concepts.definition: Use a draft model and verification to generate tokens with less inference time.

concepts.label: Vision-language-action models
concepts.definition: Map visual and language inputs to actions, often for embodied tasks.

concepts.label: World models
concepts.definition: Predict environment states or outcomes to support reasoning and action.

concepts.label: Model-based reinforcement learning
concepts.definition: Use a learned or given environment model to plan or improve a policy.

concepts.label: Meta-learning
concepts.definition: Learn how to adapt to new tasks through shared learning structure.

concepts.label: Belief-desire-intention agents
concepts.definition: Represent agent behavior through beliefs, goals, and intentions.

concepts.label: Agents for games and puzzles
concepts.definition: Use agents to act in game environments or solve interactive puzzles.

concepts.label: Query rewriting and expansion
concepts.definition: Change or extend a search query to retrieve more useful evidence.

concepts.label: Travel and flight assistants
concepts.definition: Use agents to plan trips, book travel, or support flight operations.

concepts.label: Trading and financial assistants
concepts.definition: Use agents to analyze financial information or support trading decisions.

concepts.label: Strategic and social agent behavior
concepts.definition: Study cooperation, coordination, persuasion, and social interaction among agents.

concepts.label: Theory of mind
concepts.definition: Represent or infer another actor's beliefs, goals, or knowledge.

concepts.label: Moral judgment and ethical behavior
concepts.definition: Study moral choices, value alignment, and differences between stated judgments and actions.

concepts.label: Behavioral experiments on agents
concepts.definition: Use controlled tasks to measure observable agent behavior.

concepts.label: Social simulation with agents
concepts.definition: Use interacting agents to model communities, groups, or societies.

concepts.label: Emergent communication and social norms
concepts.definition: Study conventions and norms that arise from repeated agent interaction.

concepts.label: Model collapse and synthetic-data risks
concepts.definition: Study how repeated training on generated data can reduce quality or diversity.

concepts.label: Recursive and self-modifying agents
concepts.definition: Use recursive agent calls or agent-directed changes to system behavior.

concepts.label: Mechanistic interpretability
concepts.definition: Study internal model features and computations that cause behavior.

concepts.label: Activation patching and causal intervention
concepts.definition: Change internal activations to test their causal effect on model output.

concepts.label: Sparse autoencoders for feature discovery
concepts.definition: Learn sparse features from model activations to inspect internal representations.

concepts.label: Model circuit analysis
concepts.definition: Identify groups of model components that implement specific computations.

concepts.label: Metacognition and self-knowledge
concepts.definition: Study how agents estimate, monitor, or describe their own knowledge and limits.

concepts.label: Cognitive analysis of agents
concepts.definition: Compare behavioral, representational, and mechanistic evidence about agent capabilities.

concepts.label: Consciousness and agency theories
concepts.definition: Discuss theories and evidence about consciousness in model-based agents.
